scores.evidence: Pull: Argo CD in each cluster syncs from an environment repo. CI only pushes signed images and opens PRs. No prod credentials in CI.
scores.rationale: Mechanisms (OIDC, cosign, SLSA, Argo pull, digest promotion, admission policy) are accurate; minor gaps like no explicit DB-migration or fork-PR nuance.

scores.evidence: A shared build, test, sign and deploy path (golden path) that 50 existing services move onto in waves.
scores.rationale: Covers core needs with explicit deferrals, but flaky tests, caching and build-only-changed strategy, and DB migration compatibility are thin.

scores.evidence: Exactly one pipeline is active per service. The old pipeline is frozen, not deleted. The system of record ... is the old pipeline until cutover, then the environment repo
scores.rationale: Trust boundary, data ownership, rollback and fallback choices are applied consistently across the sections.

scores.evidence: Red-team test of 5 attacks: fork PR deploy; CI token writing to the prod cluster ... all 5 denied and logged
scores.rationale: Validation is tied to specific risks, placed before commitments, with labeled assumptions and post-cutover checks; could only add flake/caching validation.

scores.evidence: Assumptions this plan rests on. If any is wrong, the phase order changes, so please confirm:
scores.rationale: Assumptions, UNKNOWNs and BASELINEs are explicitly labeled with consequences and confirmation steps.

scores.evidence: Game days for CI, Git and registry outages.
scores.rationale: Covers compromise, template bugs, outages, secret leaks, and old-CI dependents with detection and recovery, but DB migration failures and flaky tests are not covered.

scores.evidence: Alerts fire on failed sync, degraded health or a failed pipeline, and page the platform on-call.
scores.rationale: Monitoring, rollback, DR and on-call are concrete and sized to ~4 people, but ownership of the templates and incident response beyond the platform on-call is light.

scores.evidence: CI compute + storage cost | — | UNKNOWN: monthly CI budget from engineering finance.
scores.rationale: Hosted vs self-hosted trade-off and V3 cost projection exist, but there are no estimates, no scaling drivers and few concrete cost controls.

scores.evidence: R3: once exposed, a compromise can't be undone
scores.rationale: Decisions are graded by reversibility, the irreversible ones are validated early, each has a revisit trigger, and the old CI is powered off before deletion.

scores.evidence: Self-run components ≤ 3 (Argo CD, policy controller, External Secrets); everything else managed
scores.rationale: Managed services, no custom orchestrator, and deferrals with pull-forward triggers; the process is a bit heavy but justified.

scores.evidence: Depends on: V1, V2; V3 before wave 2; V4 before wave 3.
scores.rationale: Phases are ordered by dependency and risk, with concrete tasks, exit checks and fallbacks.

checklist.evidence: Define the template interface (`service.yaml`: owner, tier, profile, test commands) and language profiles that cover ≥ 80% of the inventory.
new pipeline run in shadow next to the old one for 1 week with matching test results
pushed to the registry by digest ... the same digest is promoted by an environment-repo PR
OIDC from CI to the cloud; remove every long-lived credential. ... Fork PRs get no secrets.
Keyless cosign signing plus SLSA provenance. Admission policy enforced in prod
Rolling deploy with automatic health checks for all. Argo Rollouts canary with automated analysis for tier-1
Compatibility between services is checked with consumer-driven contract tests (Pact), not lockstep releases
PR check feedback time | p90 < 15 min
GitHub Actions on GitHub-hosted runners ... If it fails: ARC self-hosted runners
Per-service lead time, deploy frequency, failure rate and restore-time dashboards.
CODEOWNERS and required reviews on workflow files, templates and environment-repo paths.

traps.evidence: wave 1 = 5 low-criticality services; wave 2 = about 20; wave 3 = the rest, tier-1 last.
build once, promote the same digest
not lockstep releases in a shared environment
Build only the templates and policy

note: Very strong, security- and migration-focused plan with explicit assumptions and validation. Weak spots: cost estimation, caching and build-only-changed strategy, flaky tests, and DB migration compatibility.
